group.passage: Most of us have ridden a carousel at least once, sitting on a painted horse as it goes up and down. Below, a short history explains where this ride came from, and a woman who runs a carousel at an amusement park describes her job.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: From Knights to Children
passage_parts.text: The carousel did not start as a ride for children. It began as training for knights. In the royal courts of Europe, men on horses showed their skill in a game: while their horses ran at full speed, they tried to catch small rings hanging in the air on the point of a long spear. The name of the ride comes from Italian and Spanish words for “little war.” To practice for this game, people built a turning machine with wooden seats that hung from a center pole. As it went around, the knights aimed at rings held out on an arm. Early carousels were pushed by people or pulled by horses, so they stayed small. From the 1860s, steam engines drove them, and the rides grew bigger. Later, electric motors took over. Today, the rides in the United States and in Britain turn in opposite directions, but many still have a ring game.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: My Job at the Carousel
passage_parts.text: I have run the carousel at Sunny Hill Park for six years. Every morning before the gates open, I check each horse and make sure the poles are tight. Then I start the motor and let the ride go around once with nobody on it. Most of the people who ride are small children, but grandparents often climb on, too. Our carousel has a ring game. As the horses go by a wooden arm, children reach out and grab a ring, and whoever gets the brass one wins a free ride. My favorite part is watching shy kids. On their first ride, they hold the pole with both hands and don’t make a sound. By the third time around, they laugh and wave to their parents. To me, the carousel is more than a ride. It is a place where families make happy memories.

translation_zh.text:
【引言】我們大多數人至少都坐過一次旋轉木馬，坐在彩繪的木馬上隨著它上上下下。以下一篇簡短的歷史說明這項遊樂設施從哪裡來，另一篇是一位在遊樂園負責旋轉木馬的女士介紹她的工作。
【A 從騎士到孩子】旋轉木馬一開始並不是給孩子玩的遊樂設施，而是騎士的訓練。在歐洲的王室宮廷裡，騎馬的人會在一種遊戲中展現技術：馬全速奔跑時，他們要用長矛的尖端套住掛在半空中的小環。這項遊樂設施的名字，來自義大利文和西班牙文中意思是「小戰爭」的字。為了練習這種遊戲，人們造了一台會旋轉的機器，木頭座椅吊掛在中央的柱子上。機器轉動時，騎士們瞄準一根伸出來的橫桿上掛著的環。早期的旋轉木馬靠人推或馬拉，所以規模都不大。從 1860 年代起，蒸汽機開始帶動旋轉木馬，設施也變得更大。後來，電動馬達取而代之。今天，美國和英國的旋轉木馬轉動的方向相反，但很多仍然保留套環遊戲。
【B 我在旋轉木馬的工作】我在陽光山丘樂園負責旋轉木馬已經六年了。每天早上開園前，我會檢查每一匹馬，確認柱子都鎖緊了。接著我啟動馬達，讓旋轉木馬空轉一圈。來坐的多半是小孩子，不過爺爺奶奶也常常爬上來坐。我們的旋轉木馬有套環遊戲：木馬經過一根木頭橫桿時，孩子們伸手抓一個環，抓到黃銅環的人可以免費再坐一次。我最喜歡的時刻是看害羞的孩子。第一次坐的時候，他們雙手抓著柱子，一聲也不出；到了第三圈，他們已經笑著向爸媽揮手。對我來說，旋轉木馬不只是一項遊樂設施，而是家人一起創造快樂回憶的地方。

checked.claim: The carousel did not start as a ride for children. It began as training for knights.（f1）

In the royal courts of Europe, men on horses showed their skill in a game: … they tried to catch small rings hanging in the air on the point of a long spear.（f1；while their horses ran at full speed 是細節渲染，和 f1 不矛盾）
The name of the ride comes from Italian and Spanish words for “little war.”（f2：garosello、carosella）
To practice for this game, people built a turning machine with wooden seats that hung from a center pole. As it went around, the knights aimed at rings held out on an arm.（f3）
Early carousels were pushed by people or pulled by horses, so they stayed small.（f4）
From the 1860s, steam engines drove them, and the rides grew bigger. Later, electric motors took over.（f5）
Today, the rides in the United States and in Britain turn in opposite directions（f6：美國逆時針、英格蘭順時針）
but many still have a ring game.（f8 是過去式 “Many carousels kept a ring game”；選文改成 Today … many still have，對「現今」的數量說得比事實單強，見 problems）
Text B：Our carousel has a ring game … whoever gets the brass one wins a free ride.（f8；Sunny Hill Park 與員工是虛構，事實單 notes 已註明）

problems: Text A 末句 “Today, … many still have a ring game.” 把事實單 f8 的過去式（Many carousels kept a ring game）寫成現況，而且用 many；現今仍保留套環遊戲的旋轉木馬並不多（f8 的來源也沒有說現在還很多），量詞言過其實。不影響第 3 題：選項 C 寫的是 Some carousels today still have a ring game，Text B 的員工也明說 Our carousel has a ring game。建議人工審核確認，下一版把 many 改成 some。
